## 2. Step 2 — the post's quotations (method and result)

Opened `process-lessons.md` at 02:05 IST (after §1 above). A script (scratchpad `quotes.py`, `tags.py`) extracted every string in quotation marks from the study (267), searched each in `page.txt` (curly quotes normalized; pieces split at "…"), and for every hit compared the post section it occurs in ([I] l. 1–16, [W] l. 17–29, [K] l. 30–56, [T] l. 57–71, [O] l. 72–82) with the next tag in the study's line. Result: every passage tagged [I]/[W]/[K]/[T]/[O] occurs verbatim in `page.txt`, in the tagged section. The only textual differences are conventional: nested double quotes rendered as single quotes (`'one unproven lemma.'`, `'good agreement.'`, `'footgun'`) and one bracketed edit of record text (`do[es]`). No misquotation of the post. The 141 non-hits are quotations of the record (Step 3) or single words. What the quotations get wrong is framing, not text: see F1 (P12 and §0 "one sentence"), F2 (§0 "What the post does not contain"), F9 (the P9 heading puts a phrase that is not the post's inside quotation marks), F10 (P8 dates a December experiment to "the first project"; P9 turns the post's "in almost all cases" into "every time").

**Summary of Step 3(b).** All five evidence files pass a sample of at least three rows each re-derived from the record; none fails as a table, so no block is FIX-FIRST merely for leaning on an evidence file. The defects are in how the study reads them (F3–F8, F13) and in four omissions of the files themselves (B1's 37 %, B1's mixed S8 list, B2's stamp list missing Sessions 16, 20, 36, A's c9).
